notes: Hermes `/new` (alias /reset) rotation, in-process. Hermes is a presession adapter: it gets a processlifecycle Scanner with WithCommandLineMatch (core/cmd/irrlichd/wiring.go:103), so a transient proc-<PID> row is born ready at launch and hands off to the store-keyed session id once the sessions row is INSERTed. Every post-birth phase is anchored to the REAL session, never the proc row. `/new now` (the _DESTRUCTIVE_SKIP_TOKENS inline-skip, cli.py:10803) rotates without the destructive-slash modal: cli.py:7574's new_session() ends the old row (ended_at + end_reason='new_session', hermes_state.py:4326) and INSERTs the new row IMMEDIATELY (cli.py:7707) — so unlike opencode the post-reset id exists before the next prompt. old_session_ended asserts the #169 same-PID cleanup (pid_manager.go:548-613) retiring the pre-reset row once the post-reset session is PID-bound to the same hermes chat process. PROVISIONAL: no hermes recording exists yet for any scenario; every phase here is derived from the adapter + shared-services source, and `record` settles it. No cost_nonzero assertion — hermes prices via aliases.go and the store's models are not in it.

text: Pre-session row (proc-<PID>) appears in ready shortly after `hermes chat` launches under tmux

The store-keyed session id (YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<6hex>) appears in ready — the proc-<PID> row hands off to the real session once hermes INSERTs its sessions row. Unbounded: the REPL boot loads its toolsets/skills before the first prompt can land.
First user prompt drives ready → working on the store-keyed session
First turn completes back to ready on the same session id — hermes' finish_reason='stop' is an explicit turn boundary, no idle heuristic
Acceptance: 'New session appears in ready with a new session_id' — after /new the store carries a fresh id never seen before, INSERTed at reset time

Acceptance: 'Old session disappears' — the pre-reset id is retired once the post-reset session claims the same PID (same-PID cleanup, #169). Bounded relative to the new session's birth so the visible overlap window stays short.
Second user prompt drives the NEW session ready → working (must NOT match a stale working transition on the pre-reset id)
Second turn completes back to ready on the new session — final state ready
